summary:
As part of coursework for an upper-year philsophy course, I developed this paper to explore and motivate the need for interpretability in LLMs.

Rather than approaching LLMs through a purely technical or empirical lens, the paper offers a critical philosophical evaluation of their interface design — especially the now-ubiquitous chat format — and argues that interpretability should be understood as the root concern from which other moral issues like fairness, privacy, and explainability stem. Drawing on examples from both historical and contemporary human-computer interaction, the paper critiques how the current interface layer not only obscures the reasoning of the underlying models but also fosters misleading anthropomorphization and ad hoc moral interventions.
title: Coursework: Motivating Interpretability
